title: Two-dimensional galaxy cluster shapes using lensing data: a simulated analysis
comment: submitted to A&A, 16 pages, 9 figures; comments are welcome
summary: Context. Cluster morphology reflects assembly history and dynamical state. High-resolution weak lensing can reveal departures from spherical symmetry, but its ability to recover two-dimensional shapes remains less explored. Aims. We assess how reliably weak lensing recovers projected cluster morphology and its dependence on orientation and dynamical state. We also compare large-scale weak-lensing morphology with that traced by strong lensing near the cluster centre. Methods. We study three clusters at $z=0.22$ from The Three Hundred Project, representing relaxed, mildly disturbed and unrelaxed systems. For each, we consider three random projections and three along the principal axes of the mass tensor. For each projection, we generate 128 weak-lensing catalogues with a source density of 30 arcmin$^{-2}$ and intrinsic ellipticity dispersion $σ_ε=0.3$. We constrain mass and concentration from one-dimensional NFW and BMO fits, then recover ellipticity, position angle and centre using a two-dimensional elliptical NFW model. We also measure morphology from true convergence maps, Kaiser \& Squires reconstructions and strong-lensing tangential critical lines. Results. Recovered parameters depend on orientation and dynamical state. The relaxed cluster has similar inner and large-scale shapes, whereas disturbed systems appear more elliptical centrally. Two-dimensional weak-lensing modelling recovers the projected mass orientation despite source sampling and shape noise. Kaiser \& Squires reconstructions recover the position angle well but favour rounder mass distributions. Centroid offsets are larger in unrelaxed systems. Conclusions. Combining weak- and strong-lensing morphology probes cluster structure across physical scales and offers a promising way to investigate morphology and dynamical state.

title: Constraining the Inner Dark Matter Profiles of Strong-Lensing Galaxy Clusters
summary: We present mass modeling of three strong lensing galaxy clusters found in the Dark Energy Survey utilizing Hubble Space Telescope imaging for lens modeling, and complementary constraints from Chandra X-ray observations. All three clusters are relaxed and have giant arc or ring lens structures ideal for constraints on the dark matter distribution. The strong lens modeling and X-ray temperatures yield consistent total cluster mass estimates. We find these clusters have best-fit X-ray temperatures of $2.7 - 6.2$ keV and total masses of M$_{200} = (1-6) \times 10^{14} M_{\odot}$. Our lens models parameterize dark matter distribution with a generalized Navarro-Frenk-White (GNFW) density profile. While the GNFW profile allows the inner dark matter slope to vary, we find in all cases that the inner slopes are consistent with the standard NFW density profile $γ^{DM} = 1$. The X-ray surface brightness distributions for all three clusters are generally symmetric with no significant substructure, supporting the conclusion that these are relaxed clusters. In addition, we find generally low values of the external shear magnitude with median values ranging $|γ^{ext}| = 0.04-0.09$ and consistent with zero for two of the clusters.

artifacts.abstract_zh: 我们利用哈勃空间望远镜成像进行透镜建模，并结合钱德拉X射线观测的补充约束，对暗能量巡天中发现的三颗强透镜星系团进行了质量建模。这三颗星系团均处于弛豫状态，并具有巨弧或环状透镜结构，非常适合用于约束暗物质分布。强透镜建模与X射线温度给出的星系团总质量估计一致。我们发现这些星系团的最佳拟合X射线温度为 $2.7 - 6.2$ keV，总质量为 M$_{200} = (1-6) \times 10^{14} M_{\odot}$。我们的透镜模型用广义Navarro-Frenk-White（GNFW）密度剖面参数化暗物质分布。虽然GNFW剖面允许内区暗物质斜率变化，但我们发现所有情况下内区斜率均与标准NFW密度剖面 $γ^{DM} = 1$ 一致。三颗星系团的X射线表面亮度分布总体对称，没有显著子结构，支持它们是弛豫星系团的结论。此外，我们发现外部剪切幅度普遍较低，中值为 $|γ^{ext}| = 0.04-0.09$，其中两颗星系团与零一致。
artifacts.conclusion_zh: 基于现有摘要的AI结论：强透镜与X射线联合分析表明，这三个弛豫星系团的暗物质内区分布符合标准NFW剖面，外部剪切影响较弱，支持将此类巨弧星系团作为暗物质分布研究的理想探针。

title: SN Ares: A Strongly Lensed Type IIb Supernova at $\mathbf{z=1.276}$ with a Predicted 70-Year Time Delay
comment: 22 pages, 12 figures, 4 tables, submitted to ApJ
summary: We present the discovery of supernova (SN) Ares, a strongly lensed supernova at $z_{\rm spec}=1.276\pm0.002$ in a massive, triply imaged host galaxy behind the MACS J0308.9+2645 galaxy cluster. JWST/NIRSpec spectroscopy spanning the rest-frame optical to NIR of Ares reveals helium features at $5876\,\mathring{\mathrm{A}}$, $7065\,\mathring{\mathrm{A}}$, and $10830\,\mathring{\mathrm{A}}$, as well as H$α$ and Pa$β$. A comparison to local core-collapse SN spectra and light curves leads to a classification of SN Ares as a Type IIb supernova, the highest-redshift member of its class spectroscopically identified. A comparison to local SN IIb light curves provides a phase estimate for the spectrum of $34_{-9}^{+10}$ rest-frame days post-radioactive peak, providing a unique view into a high-redshift stripped-envelope supernova in its late-photospheric evolution. A lens model of the cluster constructed using recent JWST data indicates that SN Ares is the first image to arrive and will reappear in two future images near the center of the cluster plane in $\gtrsim 70$ years, with predicted magnifications of $\sim5\times$ and $\sim1.5\times$. Planned JWST/NIRSpec Multi-Object Spectroscopy of the cluster will allow for more detailed modeling of the lensed system for tighter constraints on the time delay and magnifications, as well as a template spectrum at the location of SN Ares.

title: Neglecting Dynamical Microlensing Can Bias Accretion Disk Size Measurements at the Population Level
summary: Microlensing of strongly lensed quasars probes unresolved accretion disks, but many inference methods use static magnification maps with fixed relative microlens positions. Using the GPU-accelerated simulator Microcaustics, we generate ten-year multiband light curves for three quadruply lensed quasar configurations. We compare dynamical microlensing with independent microlens motions against coherent bulk motion, and a microlens mass distribution against equal masses, keeping the velocity distribution of individual microlenses and mean mass fixed. We infer population disk sizes using ridge regression on the means and lower and upper scatters of ten variability and event metrics. We measure biases by applying models trained with simplified physics to simulations including both effects. Models trained on coherent motion interpret the additional variability from evolving caustics as smaller disks. For populations of 128 independent realizations, jointly inferred radii are consistently smaller by 6-28%. Microlens dynamics increase caustic-crossing rates pooled across all four macroimages by 5-15% and r-band high-magnification-event (HME) rates by 13-25%, while shortening median HME durations by 4-12%. Omitting the mass distribution produces configuration-dependent disk-size offsets from -12% to +5%. Including the mass distribution decreases caustic-crossing rates by 6-8% and HME rates by 6-12%. It also narrows the spread of ten-year averaged microlensing time-delay differences between macroimages by a median of 9-12% per system, while microlens dynamics have a smaller, image-pair-dependent effect. These results demonstrate the importance of microlens dynamics for population disk-size inference and motivate simulations that include dynamical microlensing and a microlens mass distribution.

title: Multiphase Gas Structure in JWST Little Red Dots
summary: JWST has uncovered a population of compact high-redshift galaxies, 'little red dots' (LRDs), exhibiting broad Balmer emission lines that often show narrow absorption features and strong Balmer breaks - spectral signatures attributed to dense gas surrounding rapidly growing black holes, but whose small-scale structure remains unknown. A striking feature of LRD spectra is that the H$β$ absorption is systematically deeper than H$α$, yet in any homogeneous gas this ordering is physically impossible. Here we model the H$α$ and H$β$ line profiles using radiative transfer simulations for 11 LRDs with JWST sensitive high resolution spectroscopy, and independently constrain the $n=2$ hydrogen column density, $N_{\rm HI,\mathit{n}=2}$, from the Balmer-break continuum. We find that the $N_{\rm HI,\mathit{n}=2}$ from H$α$ in a homogeneous medium cannot reproduce the observed H$β$ absorption in several objects, and that this $N_{\rm HI,\mathit{n}=2}$ typically falls two orders of magnitude below the lower bound set by the Balmer break. Both tensions are simultaneously resolved by a multiphase medium of dense clumps within diffuse hot ionized gas. This multiphase gas structure is a necessary ingredient for any viable LRD model, regardless of the nature of the central engine.

title: How Steep is your Dust? Direct Measurements of Nebular Attenuation Curves at Cosmic Noon with JWST
comment: 17 pages, 13 figures (+Appendix 3 pages, 6 figures), submitted to MNRAS, comments welcome
summary: Tracing the shape of the nebular attenuation curve, which is crucial for accurately measuring intrinsic emission-line fluxes, has proven challenging both in the local universe and at high redshift. Here we present nebular dust attenuation curves measured directly for 24 star-forming galaxies ($9.3<\log(\rm M{\star}/M_\odot)<11.1$) at cosmic noon ($1.8<z<3.3$) from the Blue Jay survey. Using deep JWST/NIRSpec spectra, we measure up to eight hydrogen recombination lines from H$δ$ to Pa$β$ per galaxy and find little diversity in the curve shape, with most galaxies agreeing with the \citet{calzetti_dust_2000} attenuation curve. For over $90\%$ of the sample, the nebular reddening from the Balmer lines is consistent with that from the Paschen lines. Using \texttt{Prospector} spectral energy distribution (SED) fits, we obtain the stellar reddening and find that the difference between stellar and nebular reddening increases with stellar mass, and that each reddening measurement is independent of inclination, which disagrees with the two-component dust model. We then measure the impact of using the derived nebular attenuation curve or a literature curve when determining metallicity using the strong-line method, and find that for some diagnostics (e.g., S32, S3, S23, and S3O3), the difference can be as large as $5σ$. Caution is needed when using these diagnostics if the nebular attenuation curve cannot be directly measured, since the resulting uncertainty can exceed the measurement uncertainty on the emission-line fluxes even with high signal-to-noise Balmer decrement measurements. These results show that the shape of the nebular attenuation curve is poorly understood and that constraining it is important for reducing systematic uncertainty in galaxy measurements.

title: Co-evolution of AGN and Host Galaxies across Cosmic Time Using JWST data
summary: Understanding the complex co-evolution of active galactic nuclei (AGN) and their host galaxies across cosmic time remains a fundamental challenge, particularly in identifying how the physical drivers of galaxy diversity evolve from the early Universe to the present day. To understand this, we use a multi-wavelength JWST catalog of 2,709 sources cross-matched from the SMILES and JWST Advanced Deep Extragalactic Survey (JADES) surveys, spanning lookback times from 0.8 to 12.9 Gyr ($0.05 <z <6$). Using Pearson correlation matrix, we find AGN luminosity ($L_{\mathrm{AGN}}$) strongly correlates ($\sim0.8$) with star formation rate (SFR) and dust luminosity ($L_{\mathrm{dust}}$), weakly correlates ($\sim0.5$) with stellar mass ($M_\star$) and anti-correlates ($\sim -0.4$) with star formation history (SFH) duration and stellar age (Age$_\star$). However, the apparent anti-correlation observed between galaxy age and AGN luminosity is driven by cosmic time rather than by a direct physical connection. Using Principal Component Analysis (PCA), we find that galaxy diversity is fundamentally governed by two principal components: AGN and galaxy activity, and stellar age. At higher redshifts, AGN accretion, star formation, and dust emission are tightly synchronized, reflecting gas-rich conditions in the early Universe. In contrast, the present Universe exhibits a clear bimodal structure in host-dominated systems ($f_{\mathrm{AGN}} \leq 0.2$), separating quiescent and star-forming galaxies. Our results demonstrate that AGN luminosity is primarily governed by the host galaxy's current cold-gas supply, of which recent star formation is a close observational tracer, with galaxy mass setting the overall potential. This highlights a co-evolution scenario in which black hole growth and star formation are tightly linked, particularly at early cosmic epochs.

AI.method: 使用SMILES与JADES交叉匹配得到的2,709个源的多波段JWST星表（回望时间0.8–12.9 Gyr，0.05<z<6）；采用Pearson相关矩阵分析AGN光度与SFR、尘埃光度、恒星质量、SFH时标与恒星年龄的相关性；再用主成分分析（PCA）提取主导星系多样性的主成分，并按AGN分数（f_AGN≤0.2的宿主主导系统）与红移分层比较。
AI.result: L_AGN与SFR和L_dust强相关（~0.8），与M_star弱相关（~0.5），与SFH时标和Age_star呈弱反相关（~-0.4）；但年龄—AGN光度的表观反相关由宇宙时间而非直接物理联系驱动。PCA显示星系多样性由两个主成分（AGN与星系活动、恒星年龄）支配。高红移处AGN吸积、恒星形成与尘埃辐射高度同步；近邻宇宙中宿主主导系统呈现宁静/恒星形成双峰结构。

artifacts.abstract_zh: 理解活动星系核（AGN）与其宿主星系在宇宙时间尺度上的复杂共同演化仍然是一个基本挑战，特别是在识别星系多样性的物理驱动因素如何从早期宇宙演化到今天这一方面。为了理解这一点，我们使用了一个多波段JWST目录，包含2709个源，这些源交叉匹配自SMILES和JWST高级深河外巡天（JADES），回溯时间从0.8到12.9 Gyr（$0.05 <z <6$）。使用皮尔逊相关矩阵，我们发现AGN光度（$L_{\mathrm{AGN}}$）与恒星形成率（SFR）和尘埃光度（$L_{\mathrm{dust}}$）强相关（$\sim0.8$），与恒星质量（$M_\star$）弱相关（$\sim0.5$），并与恒星形成历史（SFH）持续时间和恒星年龄（Age$_\star$）反相关（$\sim -0.4$）。然而，观测到的星系年龄与AGN光度之间的表观反相关是由宇宙时间驱动的，而不是由直接的物理联系驱动的。使用主成分分析（PCA），我们发现星系多样性从根本上由两个主成分控制：AGN和星系活动，以及恒星年龄。在更高红移处，AGN吸积、恒星形成和尘埃发射紧密同步，反映了早期宇宙中富含气体的条件。相比之下，当今宇宙在宿主主导系统（$f_{\mathrm{AGN}} \leq 0.2$）中表现出明显的双峰结构，区分了宁静星系和恒星形成星系。我们的结果表明，AGN光度主要受宿主星系当前冷气体供给支配，近期恒星形成是一个紧密的观测示踪，星系质量设定了整体势。这突显了一个共同演化场景，其中黑洞增长和恒星形成紧密相连，特别是在早期宇宙时期。
artifacts.conclusion_zh: AGN光度主要受宿主星系当前冷气体供给支配（近期恒星形成是紧密的观测示踪），星系质量设定整体势；黑洞增长与恒星形成紧密耦合，尤其在早期宇宙，支持共同演化图景。

title: Measuring the magnetization profiles of galaxy groups and clusters
summary: Magnetic fields are vital in determining the physical conditions of baryons in massive halos. They are, however, notoriously difficult to observe. This impacts problems from our understanding of galaxy formation, to the observed deficit in the amplitude of thermal Sunyaev-Zel'dovich (tSZ) power spectrum that affects cosmological inferences. Although Faraday rotation measures (RMs) offer a direct probe of magnetic fields, it weights magnetic fields by the free-electron density. Several probes of free electrons, including fast radio burst (FRB) dispersion measures (DMs) and kinematic SZ (kSZ) effect, are now maturing into precision tools. We combine RM$^2$ stacks from SPICE-RACS around DESI galaxy groups and ROSAT clusters with optical depth profiles constrained jointly by the FRB DM-redshift relation and the kSZ effect, and obtain 95% upper limits on the rms line-of-sight magnetic field of $<3.9$-$11.6~μ$G ($<2.3$-$6.4~μ$G) in groups (clusters) for a 10~kpc coherence length. Combining these with thermal pressure profiles inferred from tSZ-shear cross-correlations, we obtain 95% lower limits on the plasma $β$ of $>0.31$ ($>11$) in groups (clusters). Although current constraints are only limits, we forecast a first detection with larger datasets from the Deep Synoptic Array (DSA). We present the first forecast of the DSA RM grid density ($\sim365$ RMs deg$^{-2}$), which when combined with 10$^4$ FRBs would measure the field in groups to $3$-$13\%$ precision, compared to current constraints of $38$-$75\%$. Although the interpretation of current measurements remains challenging owing to depolarization along turbulent halo sightlines and the unknown coherence length, larger samples and DSA/Square Kilometer Array observations may resolve these uncertainties by measuring polarization-fraction profiles and the RM structure function using extended radio sources, respectively.

AI.tldr: We combine SPICE-RACS Faraday rotation measure stacks around DESI groups and ROSAT clusters with electron optical-depth profiles constrained by FRB dispersion measures and the kSZ effect, placing 95% upper limits of <3.9-11.6 μG (<2.3-6.4 μG) on the rms line-of-sight magnetic field in groups (clusters) at 10 kpc coherence length, and lower limits on plasma β of >0.31 (>11).
AI.motivation: Magnetic fields set the physical conditions of baryons in massive halos but are notoriously hard to observe, affecting galaxy formation understanding and the tSZ power-spectrum amplitude deficit relevant to cosmology. RM alone weights fields by free-electron density, so independent electron probes are needed to break the degeneracy.
AI.method: Combine RM^2 stacks from SPICE-RACS around DESI galaxy groups and ROSAT clusters with optical-depth profiles jointly constrained by the FRB DM-redshift relation and the kSZ effect; further combine with thermal pressure profiles from tSZ-shear cross-correlations to constrain plasma β. Also forecast DSA RM grid density (~365 RMs deg^-2) combined with 10^4 FRBs.
AI.result: 95% upper limits on rms line-of-sight field of <3.9-11.6 μG in groups and <2.3-6.4 μG in clusters (10 kpc coherence length); 95% lower limits on plasma β of >0.31 (groups) and >11 (clusters). Forecast: DSA+10^4 FRBs would measure group fields to 3-13% precision vs. current 38-75%.
AI.conclusion: Current constraints are only limits, but larger samples promise a first detection. Interpretation remains challenged by depolarization along turbulent sightlines and unknown coherence length; these may be resolved by polarization-fraction profiles and RM structure functions from extended radio sources with DSA/SKA.

title: Towards Reliably Measuring the Mass-Size Relation of Dark Matter Halos: Impact of projection, miscentering and Eddington bias
comment: 25 pages, 18 figures. Comments and feedback welcome
summary: In the conventional spherical overdensity definition of a dark matter halo, masses and radii, e.g. $M_{200{\rm m}}$ and $r_{200{\rm m}}$, are equivalent. However, halos do exhibit a physical boundary at the splashback radius $r_{\rm sp}$, which manifests as a sharp drop in density. Splashback radii are now routinely measured in stacked weak lensing profiles, but the expected trend of decreasing $r_{\rm sp}/r_{200{\rm m}}$ with mass has not been verified in observed galaxy groups or clusters. In this work, we show that several observational effects conceal the predicted mass-size relation. In particular, we quantify the impact of systematics on the mean density and lensing profiles of mock-observed halo samples, which are created by applying a realistic cluster-finding procedure to dark matter-only simulations. We reproduce the known impact of projection: preferentially observing systems in overdense regions. But, differing from previous works, we show that the same projection effect, combined with scatter in observed luminosities, causes a significant Eddington bias in the derived mass-observable relation and a complex suppression in mean density profiles over all radial scales. The magnitude of this effect is mass-dependent and coupled to the cluster-finding procedure and survey properties, making it challenging to model simply and motivating full forward-modeling of observed group and cluster samples. However, we demonstrate that a simple mitigation approach, effectively a weak lensing mass calibration, does well in approximately recovering the true mass-size relation. Finally, we show that only severe miscentering can bias the measurement of the halo size, but any miscentering can increase the measurement uncertainty.

artifacts.abstract_zh: 在暗物质晕传统的球状过密度定义中，质量和半径（例如 $M_{200{\rm m}}$ 和 $r_{200{\rm m}}$）是等价的。然而，暗晕在回溅半径 $r_{\rm sp}$ 处确实表现出物理边界，表现为密度的急剧下降。回溅半径现在已常规地在堆叠弱引力透镜剖面中测量，但预期的 $r_{\rm sp}/r_{200{\rm m}}$ 随质量下降的趋势尚未在观测到的星系群或星系团中得到验证。在这项工作中，我们表明若干观测效应掩盖了预测的质量-尺度关系。特别地，我们量化了系统误差对模拟观测暗晕样本的平均密度和透镜剖面的影响，这些样本是通过将现实的星系团查找程序应用于纯暗物质模拟而创建的。我们再现了投影的已知影响：优先观测处于过密区域的系统。但是，与之前的工作不同，我们表明相同的投影效应，结合观测光度的散布，在推导的质量-可观测量关系中引起显著的Eddington偏置，并在所有径向尺度上对平均密度剖面产生复杂的抑制。这种效应的幅度依赖于质量，并与星系团查找程序和巡天性质耦合，使其难以简单建模，并促使对观测到的星系群和星系团样本进行完整的正向建模。然而，我们证明一种简单的缓解方法，实际上是一种弱引力透镜质量定标，在近似恢复真实质量-尺度关系方面表现良好。最后，我们表明只有严重的中心错位才能偏置暗晕尺度的测量，但任何中心错位都会增加测量不确定性。
artifacts.conclusion_zh: 基于可用摘要：观测到的 $r_{\rm sp}/r_{200{\rm m}}$ 与质量的关系被多种观测效应（尤其是投影加Eddington偏置）所掩盖，需要对观测到的星系群/星系团样本进行完整的正向建模；一种简单的缓解方法——等效于弱引力透镜质量定标——可以近似恢复真实的质量-尺度关系。

title: Dark Matter and MOND successes and degeneracies in reproducing SPARC rotation curves and weak lensing data
summary: The observed rotation velocities of spiral galaxies at large scales exceed those predicted by their baryonic components, motivating the need for dark matter (DM) or Modified Newtonian Dynamics (MOND). We fit the rotation curves of 147 late-type galaxies from the SPARC database, using a suite of models including Cold Dark Matter (CDM) models with and without baryonic feedback, Warm DM, Fuzzy DM, and MOND. We also combine SPARC kinematics with weak-lensing data to extend the mean rotation curves to ~1 Mpc. On a galaxy-by-galaxy basis, the inner SPARC rotation curves marginally favour CDM models with baryonic feedback, although accounting for the uncertainties in distances and inclinations increases the degeneracy among DM-based models and MOND. All DM models predict host halo masses larger than abundance-matching expectations, with only the CDM model with baryonic feedback reducing the scatter around the mean luminosity-halo mass relation. MOND is able to reproduce the flatness of the mean galactic rotation curves on scales up to 1 Mpc, providing stellar mass-to-light ratios within observational uncertainties. In contrast, all DM models, without the contribution of mass external to the bound halo, struggle to explain the flat rotation curves. The inclusion of the current weak-lensing data tends to favour MOND over DM models, at least at the largest scales. Future observations from BIG-SPARC, the Square Kilometre Array, and most importantly, upcoming weak-lensing surveys such as EUCLID and Rubin will provide more stringent and independent tests of these competing frameworks

artifacts.abstract_zh: 大尺度上观测到的螺旋星系旋转速度超过其重子成分所预测的值，这促使人们需要暗物质（DM）或修正牛顿动力学（MOND）。我们使用包括有无重子反馈的冷暗物质（CDM）模型、温暗物质（WDM）、模糊暗物质（FDM）和MOND在内的一系列模型，拟合了SPARC数据库中147个晚型星系的旋转曲线。我们还将SPARC运动学数据与弱透镜数据结合，将平均旋转曲线扩展到约1 Mpc。在逐个星系的基础上，内部SPARC旋转曲线略微倾向于带有重子反馈的CDM模型，尽管考虑距离和倾角的不确定性会增加基于DM的模型与MOND之间的简并。所有DM模型预测的宿主晕质量都大于丰度匹配的预期，只有带有重子反馈的CDM模型减小了平均光度-晕质量关系周围的散布。MOND能够再现高达1 Mpc尺度上平均星系旋转曲线的平坦性，并提供在观测不确定性范围内的恒星质量-光度比。相比之下，所有DM模型在没有束缚晕外部质量贡献的情况下，难以解释平坦的旋转曲线。纳入当前的弱透镜数据倾向于在最大尺度上支持MOND而非DM模型。未来来自BIG-SPARC、平方公里阵列（SKA），尤其是EUCLID和Rubin等即将到来的弱透镜巡天的观测，将为这些竞争框架提供更严格和独立的检验。
artifacts.conclusion_zh: 基于现有摘要：现有数据尚不足以在暗物质与MOND之间给出决定性判别，但在最大尺度上略偏向MOND；未来BIG-SPARC、平方公里阵列（SKA），尤其是EUCLID与Rubin等弱透镜巡天将提供更严格且独立的检验。

figures.caption_en: Figure 1: The dark matter density profiles of a halo with \(\log_{10}(M_{{vir}})=11\) \({M_{\odot}}\) and \(\log_{10}(L_{[3.6]})=9.5\) \({L_{\odot}}\) . The dark blue dot-dashed, purple solid, orange densely-dashed, and yellow dashed curves plot the DC14, NFW, WDM, and FDM models respectively. The WDM model assumes a particle mass of \(m_{\chi}=1\) keV. We do not show the \(m_{\chi}=3\) keV case as it does not differ from the NFW curve for this particular halo.
figures.caption_zh: 图1：一个晕的暗物质密度分布，其 \(\log_{10}(M_{{vir}})=11\) \({M_{\odot}}\) 且 \(\log_{10}(L_{[3.6]})=9.5\) \({L_{\odot}}\) 。深蓝色点划线、紫色实线、橙色密集虚线和黄色虚线分别绘制了DC14、NFW、WDM和FDM模型。WDM模型假设粒子质量为 \(m_{\chi}=1\) keV。我们没有展示 \(m_{\chi}=3\) keV 的情况，因为对于这个特定的晕，它与NFW曲线没有区别。

figures.caption_en: Table 1: Table of the parameters defining each density profile and their associated priors for MCMC parameter estimation. Here \(\mu\) , and \(\sigma\) are the mean, and standard deviation of the log-normal distributions respectively.
figures.caption_zh: 表1：定义每个密度分布的参数及其用于MCMC参数估计的相关先验的表格。这里 \(\mu\) 和 \(\sigma\) 分别是对数正态分布的均值和标准差。

figures.caption_en: Table 2: The cut-off virial halo mass, \(M_{{H}}^{{s}}\) , and slope parameters ( \(\alpha\) , \(\beta\) , \(\gamma\) ) of the modified HMFs for the WDM, and FDM models. References: (1) Schneider et al. (2012b) , (2) Schive et al. (2016) .
figures.caption_zh: 表2：WDM和FDM模型的修正HMF的截止维里晕质量 \(M_{{H}}^{{s}}\) 和斜率参数（ \(\alpha\) , \(\beta\) , \(\gamma\) ）。参考文献：(1) Schneider et al. (2012b) , (2) Schive et al. (2016) 。

figures.caption_en: Figure 3: Left Panel: The modelled rotation curve fits of each model (coloured curves) to the LSB galaxy, DDO161, observed total rotation curve. Right Panel: The modelled rotation curve fits of each model (coloured curves) to the HSB galaxy, NGC0024, observed total rotation curve. The black data points and error bars show the observed total velocities at various radii and their corresponding \(1\sigma\) errors respectively. The bottom panels of each plot shows the residuals between each model prediction and the observed total velocity.
figures.caption_zh: 图3：左图：每个模型（彩色曲线）对LSB星系DDO161观测总旋转曲线的模型旋转曲线拟合。右图：每个模型（彩色曲线）对HSB星系NGC0024观测总旋转曲线的模型旋转曲线拟合。黑色数据点和误差棒分别显示了不同半径处观测到的总速度及其对应的 \(1\sigma\) 误差。每个图的底部面板显示了每个模型预测与观测总速度之间的残差。

figures.caption_en: Table 3: Table of the median reduced chi-square statistic, \(\chi^{2}\) , values for dark matter and MOND models, using maximum likelihood parameter estimation. The NFW and DC14 model are included with and without the Dutton and Macciò (2014) \(c_{{vir}}-M_{{vir}}\) relation as a prior on \(c_{vir}\) .
figures.caption_zh: 表3：使用最大似然参数估计的暗物质和MOND模型的中位约化卡方统计量 \(\chi^{2}\) 值表。NFW和DC14模型包括有和没有Dutton and Macciò (2014) \(c_{{vir}}-M_{{vir}}\) 关系作为 \(c_{vir}\) 先验的情况。

figures.caption_en: Figure 5: The rotation curve of UGC01281 assuming an Top Panel : NFW dark matter profile and a Bottom Panel : DC14 dark matter profile. The gas, stellar, and total velocity components from the SPARC database are represented by the blue dot-dashed line, dashed line, and data points, respectively. The blue shaded region denotes the \(1\sigma\) uncertainty in the circular velocity measurements. The total best-fit velocity, shown by the red curve, is the sum of the stellar, gas, and dark matter (orange curve) components. In the bottom panel of each plot, the yellow curve represents the residuals between the observed and modelled total RCs.
figures.caption_zh: 图5：假设上图：NFW暗物质分布和下图：DC14暗物质分布的UGC01281旋转曲线。来自SPARC数据库的气体、恒星和总速度分量分别由蓝色点划线、虚线和数据点表示。蓝色阴影区域表示圆周速度测量的 \(1\sigma\) 不确定性。红色曲线显示的总最佳拟合速度是恒星、气体和暗物质（橙色曲线）分量之和。在每个图的底部面板中，黄色曲线代表观测和建模的总RC之间的残差。
